title: Exact module evaluation and termwise derived localization at a partition object
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to the module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with pullbacks, a strict initial object $\varnothing$, and disjoint finite coproducts stable under pullback. Assume the component inclusions of every finite coproduct are a covering, including the empty covering of $\varnothing$. Fix an object $W$ such that every covering of $W$ refines a finite coproduct decomposition of $W$. Let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, $A=\mathcal O(W)$, and $E(M)=M(W)$ on module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For every small diagram $(M_i)$, its sectionwise module colimit presheaf $P(U)=\operatorname{colim}_i M_i(U)$ has $P(\varnothing)=0$ and the restriction map $P(\coprod_a U_a)\to\prod_aP(U_a)$ is an isomorphism. Its module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] has underlying sets the set sheafification, and $P(W)\to P^\#(W)$ is an $A$-linear isomorphism. Consequently $E$ preserves all small colimits and is exact (kernels are sectionwise and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels). For ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], termwise $E$ preserves cohomology and all quasi-isomorphisms, and its localization $D(E)$ is canonically the total right derived functor $RE$ [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], with the canonical right-derived unit. Explicitly, for every K-injective resolution $K\to I$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex], the map $E(K)\to E(I)$ is a quasi-isomorphism identifying the termwise model with $RE(K)$. The resulting unit comparison $A[0]\to RE(\mathcal O[0])$ is the identity on $A[0]$. These assertions allow an empty indexing category, $W=\varnothing$, and the zero coefficient ring.

proof.text: For a finite colimiting cofan, pull back the decomposition along one component. The stable coproduct cocone has initial off-diagonal components by disjointness. Define a retraction of the diagonal pullback projection by the other projection on the diagonal and the unique initial maps off the diagonal. The diagonal lift of the identity shows this retraction is the identity, so the two diagonal pullback projections agree and the component inclusion is monic. The underlying set presheaf of each module sheaf satisfies the empty-cover and finite-component-cover sheaf conditions. Mathlib Presieve.preservesProduct_of_isSheafFor therefore shows that each underlying abelian presheaf preserves finite products, including the empty product; forgetful reflection transfers preservation from sets to abelian groups.

source.place: Definitions of module sheaves; finite disjoint covering sheaf condition

proof.text: The underlying abelian presheaf of the sectionwise module colimit is a colimit of the underlying abelian presheaves: PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf preserves colimits. The pointwise colimit is naturally the flipped diagram followed by colim. The flipped diagram preserves finite products because every evaluation does. In any preadditive category, colim preserves finite products (Mathlib CategoryTheory.instPreservesFiniteProductsFunctorColimOfPreadditive, via finite biproducts). Thus the colimit abelian presheaf preserves finite products. Forget to sets and apply preservation to the opposite of any colimiting cofan to obtain the stated bijection, and to the initial object to obtain its singleton value. Empty diagrams, empty families and zero rings are included in these categorical arguments.

source.place: lemma-limits-colimits-abelian-presheaves, sectionwise colimit presentation; elementary finite direct-sum calculation

proof.text: By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], the underlying abelian sheaf of module sheafification is the abelian sheafification, with its canonical linear unit. By [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets], forgetting this abelian sheafification to sets gives the set sheafification, including the unit map. Steps 1-2 show that the underlying set presheaf of $P$ has singleton value on $\varnothing$ and sends finite coproducts to products. Apply [lem-zl-partition-refinement-sheafification] at $W$; its strictness, pullback, disjointness, covering and finite-refinement assumptions are exactly our site assumptions. It gives a bijection $P(W)\to P^\#(W)$. This map is $A$-linear by the module-sheafification definition; a bijective linear map has a linear inverse, so it is an $A$-module isomorphism, natural in the diagram.

source.place: Tag 0F63, lemma-presheaf-value-weakly-contractible; module sheafification as in sites-modules Tag 03CY

proof.text: The small-diagram colimit formula in [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] identifies $\operatorname{colim}_i M_i$ with $P^\#$. Consequently step 3 identifies the canonical map $\operatorname{colim}_i E(M_i)\to E(\operatorname{colim}_iM_i)$ with that same isomorphism. Thus $E$ preserves all small colimits, including cokernels and the initial zero object. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise], evaluation also preserves kernels. Evaluation is additive since addition of maps is sectionwise. In an abelian category, exactness means that image equals kernel; since image is the kernel of the cokernel, preservation of kernels and cokernels gives exactness of $E$. These statements also give the asserted sectionwise-kernel and sheafified-sectionwise-cokernel formulas.

For a complex $K$, put $Z^n=\ker d^n$ and $B^n=\operatorname{im}d^{n-1}$. Exactness identifies $E(Z^n)$ with $\ker E(d^n)$ and $E(B^n)$ with $\operatorname{im}E(d^{n-1})$; applying $E$ to the quotient $Z^n/B^n$ gives $E(H^nK)\cong H^n(EK)$. This identification is natural for chain maps, since all maps are induced by the kernel inclusions and quotient projections. Thus every quasi-isomorphism remains one. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to the additive exact functor $E$: it supplies its termwise localization $D(E)$ and the natural factorization $\varphi_K:D(E)(QK)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(EK)$ in the ordinary unbounded derived categories. No boundedness or preservation of injectives by $E$ is needed.

Apply lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor to E and its canonical Mathlib factorization mapDerivedCategoryFactors. Its right-derived clause supplies the specified canonical unit. Mathlib rightDerivedUnique and rightDerived_ext give existence and uniqueness of the unit-compatible comparison with any right-derived pair. For any quasi-isomorphism s:K→I, exactness implies E(s) is a quasi-isomorphism. Naturality of the arbitrary unit eta writes eta_K followed by RE(Qs) as Q(E(s)) followed by eta_I. Substitute unit compatibility at I and cancel the comparison isomorphism and the canonical factorization isomorphism; the resulting composite is precisely Q(E(s)). This argument applies in particular to every K-injective resolution and requires no existence theorem for resolutions.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; universal right-derived property and naturality of its canonical unit

proof.text: Finally $E(\mathcal O[0])=\mathcal O(W)[0]=A[0]$ termwise. The identification $RE\cong D(E)$ just obtained is compatible with the unit by [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]; therefore the composite $A[0]=Q(E\mathcal O[0])\xrightarrow{\eta_{\mathcal O[0]}}RE(\mathcal O[0])\cong D(E)(\mathcal O[0])\xrightarrow{\varphi}A[0]$ is the identity. Equivalently, in a K-injective model it is $Q(E(s))$ followed by its inverse. If $W=\varnothing$, the empty covering gives $A=0$ and every $E(M)=0$; all the displayed identities hold in the zero module category. The same arguments allow the zero coefficient ring and an empty indexing category throughout.
